chain.label: MSP had no formal flight risk evaluation program and had downgraded instrument training requirements
chain.trigger: the lack of adherence to effective risk management procedures by the MSP

chain.label: Pilot met currency requirements but was not proficient in instrument flight
chain.trigger: although the pilot met the recent-experience requirements to act as PIC under IFR, he was not proficient in instrument flight

caused_by.evidence: changes made by the MSP Aviation Command to its instrument training program about 10 months before the accident did not promote instrument proficiency

chain.label: Pilot likely less than fully alert; 16 hours awake, accident near his normal bedtime, sleep apnea risk factors
chain.trigger: the NTSB concludes that the pilot was likely less than fully alert, and fatigue may have contributed to his deficient decision-making

chain.label: DoD data communications switch failure blocked ADW and Fort Belvoir weather observations from DUAT and the HEMS weather tool
chain.trigger: a data communications switch failure at Offutt Air Force Base, Nebraska, prevented the Air Force Weather Agency (AFWA) from transmitting military alphanumeric data to the National Weather Service (NWS)

chain.label: Pilot's inadequate weather assessment: incomplete DUAT briefing without weather hazards, no required update, deteriorating trend discounted
chain.trigger: Other pertinent weather data—the low temperature/dew point spreads at ADW and College Park, the AIRMET for IFR conditions encompassing the route of flight, and the continuing deterioration of the weather conditions as the evening progressed—were either discounted by the pilot or not obtained

caused_by.evidence: the pilot was unaware that Fort Belvoir was reporting IFR conditions with a visibility of 1 1/4 miles in mist and a 0° temperature/dew point spread

chain.label: Pilot accepted the night medevac flight despite his own misgivings about the weather
chain.trigger: yeah we ought to be able to do it…we're going to try it

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's decision to accept the flight, after his inadequate assessment of the weather, contributed to the accident
had a formal flight risk evaluation program been in place at MSP before the accident, it may have resulted in the cancellation of the flight

chain.label: Flight encountered IMC en route to the hospital, could not reach PGH, and diverted to ADW for an instrument approach
chain.trigger: it's solid up here. I'd like to climb to 2,000 feet and go over to radar and shoot an approach over at Andrews

caused_by.evidence: Trooper 2 encountered instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) en route to the hospital and diverted to ADW

chain.label: Dark night with low ceilings, local fog, and no surface light reference over the wooded park
chain.trigger: At night, with low cloud ceilings, reduced visibility, and no surface light references, there were insufficient visual cues available for the pilot to establish ground reference

chain.label: Deficient ATC handling: nearly 5-hour-old ADW weather passed to the pilot, unresponsiveness, poor localizer vectoring, and no ASR approach available
chain.trigger: the weather given to the pilot had been issued at 1855 local time, almost 5 hours earlier

chain.label: Pilot believed he was not receiving the glideslope, effectively turning the ILS into a nonprecision approach
chain.trigger: I'm not picking up the glideslope

chain.label: Pilot increased the rate of descent from about 500 fpm to over 2,000 fpm, deviating below the glideslope to duck under the clouds
chain.trigger: the helicopter's rate of descent increased rapidly from about 500 feet per minute (fpm) to greater than 2,000 fpm, and Trooper 2's flightpath began to deviate below the glideslope

caused_by.evidence: the failure of the PCT controller to provide the current ADW weather information likely led the pilot to expect that he could descend below the cloud ceiling and establish visual contact with the ground at an altitude well above the MDA for the approach
once the controller denied it, the pilot still had many options available to conduct a safe landing in instrument conditions
a return to visual conditions would have relieved the pilot of the additional workload generated by instrument flight
Fatigue, in combination with the high workload the pilot was experiencing, could explain this uncharacteristically deficient decision
These conditions greatly increased the demands on the pilot since he had little recent experience in actual instrument flying

chain.label: Descent never arrested: helicopter passed through the 680-foot MDA, the 300-foot radar altimeter alert height, and the 200-foot decision height
chain.trigger: the pilot failed to adhere to instrument approach procedures when he did not arrest the helicopter's descent at the MDA

caused_by.evidence: No evidence was found to indicate that the pilot made any attempt to arrest the helicopter's descent before impact
the pilot failed to monitor the instruments likely because he was preoccupied with looking for the ground, which he could not identify before impact due to the lack of external visual cues
This lack of proficiency likely contributed to the pilot's failure to properly conduct what effectively became a nonprecision approach at night in instrument conditions

chain.label: Helicopter struck an 80-foot tree and terrain 3.2 miles north of the runway 19R threshold
chain.trigger: The helicopter was substantially damaged when it collided with trees and terrain in Walker Mill Regional Park, District Heights, Maryland

caused_by.evidence: The helicopter continued the descent, passing through the MDA for the localizer approach (407 feet agl), the alert height set on the radar altimeter (300 feet agl), and the decision height for the ILS approach (200 feet agl), before impacting trees and terrain

chain.label: Four occupants killed, one patient seriously injured
chain.trigger: The commercial pilot, one flight paramedic, one field provider, and one of two automobile accident patients being transported were killed

caused_by.evidence: The crash forces and reduction in volume of occupiable space within the cabin ... precluded survival for the cabin occupants
